children: Consumer prices in Costa Rica eased by 0.17% from the previous year in August of 2026, marking the softest deflation rate since the ongoing deflationary trend started in May of 2025 at -0.12%.
The slowdown in the decline in prices took place despite a second consecutive monthly drop in the CPI (-0.11% vs -0.47% in July).
Prices fell for transportation (-1.06%), contrary to global trends, as other Latin American economies are exposed to soaring fuel prices to a more immediate impact.
In turn, prices soared for food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.01%).

title: Costa Rica Holds Deflationary Trend
